ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: Capture-BEFORE-Resize permanently loses the SIGWINCH redraw: pipe attaches after both the capture and the resize
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: On pr/srv-first-frame the order is capture(157) → Resize(167) → pipe attach(171). bridge.Subscribe uses `pipe-pane -o` which only streams bytes emitted AFTER it attaches (stream.go:145), so every byte the pane emits in the window [capture, attach] is lost forever — and the Resize the server itself issues at :167 lands exactly inside that window, so the TUI's SIGWINCH redraw is the single most likely thing to be destroyed. The removed comment on main said the opposite is required ("Attach the pipe before the snapshot so no output between the two is lost").
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: Phone (108x96) subscribes to a live Claude Code pane sitting at host geometry 213x54. Server captures the 213-col screen, then resize-window to 108x96 → SIGWINCH → Claude Code repaints the whole screen at 108 cols → those bytes go to a pane with no pipe attached and are dropped. The pipe attaches ~10ms later. The client renders a 213-col capture inside a 108-col grid (wrapped/garbled or apparently blank right half) and, because the CLI is now idle, no further output ever arrives. Recovery requires user input. handleResize cannot fix it either: the App's next resize frame carries the same 108x96, br.Size before==after, and ws_handler.go:201 explicitly skips the corrective snapshot.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.evidence: ws_handler.go:157 `snap, err := snapshotWithCursor(c.ctx, br)`; :167 `br.Resize(c.ctx, int(s.Cols), int(s.Rows))`; :171 `ch, detach, err := br.Subscribe(c.ctx)`. bridge/stream.go:145 comment + `pipe-pane -o -t target "cat >> "+shellQuote(fifo)` — no retroactive buffer. handleResize takes the opposite order and documents why: ws_handler.go:213 "tmux reflows the pane synchronously on resize-window, so capturing right after Resize is content-correct".

ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: Re-subscribe captures the first frame in the middle of a restore-resize storm
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: c.subscribeCancel(s.Ref) at :140 runs teardownSubscription → restoreSize → paneGeometry.release, which on active→0 issues br.Resize back to the host baseline (pane_geometry.go, the `if known { br.Resize(context.Background(), cols, rows) }` branch). handleSubscribe then captures at :157 with zero settle time. So on the reconnect/replay path the capture is taken microseconds after a SIGWINCH that asked the TUI to repaint at a *different* size, and that repaint is again not in the pipe (attached at :171).
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: App backgrounds and returns → ConnectionManager.kt:778 re-sends SubscribeFrame for the same ref. Server: release → resize pane 108x96 → 213x54 (SIGWINCH, TUI starts clearing) → capture-pane immediately (catches the half-cleared or fully-cleared screen) → resize 213x54 → 108x96 (second SIGWINCH, repaint lost, pipe still not attached) → sends the half-cleared capture as the first frame. This is precisely the "回前台白屏" symptom the change was meant to remove, but only on the reconnect path — the new probe test only covers a first-time subscribe (hl092_static_alt_first_frame_probe_test.go sends exactly one Subscribe).
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.evidence: ws_handler.go:140 `c.subscribeCancel(s.Ref)`; ws_conn.go:477-485 teardownSubscription → restoreOnce → restoreSize; ws_handler.go:197-199 `sub.restoreSize = func() { geom.release(c.ctx, br, c.s.log, s.Ref) }`; pane_geometry.go release: `if g.active == 0 { ... br.Resize(context.Background(), cols, rows) }`.

ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: geometryFor/acquire is never released on handleSubscribe's error returns — pane stays at phone geometry forever
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: geom.acquire (:149) increments paneGeometry.active, but the three error returns that follow (:159 snapshot failure, :173 Subscribe failure, :184 encode failure) return without calling geom.release. active is then permanently inflated for that ref, so when the real subscribers later leave, active never reaches 0 and the last-leaver restore never runs. The new code moved the snapshot error path *earlier* (it used to be after Subscribe and at least called detach()), so the leak is now reachable before any pipe exists.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: Client subscribes to a pane that dies between resolvePane and snapshotWithCursor (or tmux times out) → server returns session_not_found at :159, active=1 forever. Client retries, succeeds, resizes the pane to 108x96, later unsubscribes → release drops active 2→1, not 0 → br.Resize back to 213x54 is never issued. The host user's tmux pane is left at phone geometry for the life of the daemon, violating 契约 2 of fix-host-pane-geometry-accounting.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.evidence: ws_handler.go:149 `_, _, _ = geom.acquire(c.ctx, br)`; :158-161 `if err != nil { c.sendError(...); return }` — no geom.release; :172-175 and :182-186 likewise. pane_geometry.go release: `if g.active <= 0 { return }` / `g.active--; if g.active == 0 { ...restore... }`.

ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: ConnMetrics is mutated concurrently by readLoop and every relay goroutine despite being documented as single-threaded
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: ConnMetrics is declared non-atomic on the stated ground that "连接自身的事件都在自己的读/写/relay goroutine 内". That is false: c.connMetrics.recordSnapshot() runs on the readLoop goroutine (via sendBinary from handleSubscribe/handleResize/handleScrollback) while c.connMetrics.recordFramesSent()/recordDrop() run on each relay goroutine (via sendMirror), and there is one relay goroutine per subscription. teardown then reads the whole struct while relays are still alive.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: Client subscribes to two panes and both stream deltas while the client sends a resize. relay#1 does FramesSent++, relay#2 does FramesSent++, readLoop does SnapshotsPushed++ on the same struct — an unsynchronized read-modify-write on int64 from three goroutines. Counts are silently wrong (the exact class of defect the 'per-conn vs process-level' P0 comment at ws_conn.go:82 was written to stop), and `go test -race` on any test that overlaps a delta with a snapshot on one connection will flag it. teardown's `cm := c.connMetrics` (ws_conn.go:232) races the relays it has not yet cancelled (cancel happens at :274).
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.evidence: sendq_metrics.go:62-64 "单线程使用（连接自身的事件都在自己的读/写/relay goroutine 内），无需原子"; ws_conn.go:305 `c.connMetrics.recordSnapshot()` inside sendBinary; ws_conn.go:318/322 `c.connMetrics.recordFramesSent()` / `recordDrop()` inside sendMirror; ws_conn.go:538 `c.sendMirror(frame)` inside relay; ws_conn.go:201 `go c.relay(...)` per subscription.

ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: SnapshotsFromSubscribe counts subscribe attempts, not first frames — it can never distinguish "快照没发" from "快照发了"
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: recordSubscribe() increments SubscribesTotal and SnapshotsFromSubscribe on adjacent lines, and handleSubscribe calls it at :128 before resolving the ref, before capturing, before sending anything. The two counters are therefore equal by construction and neither observes whether a snapshot frame was actually written. The field comment claims it is 「订阅路径推的快照帧数（handleSubscribe 首帧）」.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: A production run where every subscribe fails at :159 (pane gone) logs `total.subscribes=57 total.snapshots_from_subscribe=57` — a perfect green — while zero first frames reached any client. This is exactly the 世界A/世界B ambiguity the new probe test was written to break, and the metric that would have caught it in production is blind. Contrast recordResizeSnapshot, which is at least called on the resize path just before the send.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.evidence: sendq_metrics.go:51-54 `func (m *SendQueueMetrics) recordSubscribe() { m.SubscribesTotal.Add(1); m.SnapshotsFromSubscribe.Add(1) }`; ws_handler.go:128-129 called at the top of handleSubscribe; ws_handler.go:137 the unknown-ref return comes after it.

ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: unmarkAuthed's Store(0) clamp can zero a live client's count and park the listing loop
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: `if s.authed.Add(-1) <= 0 { s.authed.Store(0) }` is not atomic as a pair. A concurrent markAuthed that runs between the Add(-1) and the Store(0) is erased.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: Last client A drops at the same moment client B connects: A does Add(-1)→0; B does Add(1)→1 and pushes the 0→1 wake; A then Store(0). The listing loop consumes the wake, publishes once, loops, reads countAuthed()==0 and parks on wakeCh. B is authenticated and live but receives no list_delta at all until some third connection arrives — the level-1 menu silently stops updating for the whole session.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.evidence: server.go:356-360 unmarkAuthed; server.go:344-351 markAuthed sends on wakeCh only on the 0→1 transition; server.go:315-323 listingLoop parks whenever countAuthed()==0.

ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: openFIFO timeout leaves the pipe-pane cat attached and the FIFO on disk
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: Every other failure path in subscribe() removes the FIFO, and the returned detach() is what tears down `pipe-pane`. The openFIFO error path returns before detach exists and does neither: the `cat >> <fifo>` tmux pipe stays attached to the pane and the FIFO node stays in os.TempDir().
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: The 3s fifoOpenTimeout fires (the documented crashed-pipe / silent-toggle case). handleSubscribe gets the error at ws_handler.go:172, replies "cannot attach mirror", and the daemon has now leaked one FIFO file plus one tmux-owned cat process bound to a user pane. Repeat on every reconnect attempt and /tmp accumulates agentmirror-*.fifo nodes — a direct hit on the 进程卫生 / 资源有界 red lines. (Self-healing only kicks in on the *next* successful Subscribe of the same pane, via the detach-first at stream.go:141.)
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.evidence: stream.go:159-162 `reader, err := openFIFO(fifo); if err != nil { return nil, nil, err }` — compare stream.go:148-154, the pipe-pane Run() failure path, which does `_ = os.Remove(fifo)`.

ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.title: handleCloseSession blocks the connection's read loop for up to ~2.2s
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.claim: handleCloseSession runs synchronously on the readLoop goroutine (ws_conn.go:392) and spins with 50ms/200ms sleeps until closeWait (2s) elapses. No other frame from that client is parsed during the wait.
ac588cde3bc2b7b8d.failure_scenario: User closes a pane whose process ignores SIGTERM. For the next ~2.2s the same connection's subscribe / input / resize frames sit unread in the socket buffer: typing feels frozen and, if the user backgrounds and returns during it, the re-subscribe is delayed past the App's own timeout. Nothing in the protocol tells the client the connection is busy rather than dead.

ab2c3d5995849e4ef.title: buildSnapshot 每个 session 各 fork 一次全量 ps：N 席位 → 每 2s tick N+1 次全表 ps（卡顿引入行）
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.claim: dc9aab11b 把 `buildSnapshot(c)` 改成 `buildSnapshot(c, s.identifyProvider)`，循环里对每个 session 调一次 `s.identifyProvider(pid)` → `procFinder.Identify` → `f.snapshot([]int{pid})`。procFinder 的缓存键是「本次请求的 pid 集合」(`paneSetKey`)，单 pid 的键与 filterModel 刚用 `IdentifySet(全部pid)` 存下的键必然不同（N≥2 时），所以每一次 Identify 都是缓存 miss + 覆盖 paneKey → 每个 session 各 fork 一次 `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,comm=` 并解析全机进程表。改前每次 rebuild 只有 1 次 IdentifySet，键稳定 + 10s TTL ⇒ 实测 5 个连续 tick 内 0 次重新 fork。
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.failure_scenario: 手机客户端保持连接 + 主机上 N 个受管 pane（多 workspace 多 session）。listingLoop 每 2s 调 rebuildCatalog：filterModel 先做 1 次 IdentifySet（1 次 ps），buildSnapshot 再做 N 次 Identify（N 次 ps），每次 ps 在本机 906 个进程下实测约 48ms。N=10 → 每 tick 11 次 ps；N=30 → 每 tick 31 次 ps ≈ 1.5s 墙钟，占满 2s 周期的 3/4，daemon 持续高 CPU + 持续 fork 风暴。改前是「每 10s 1 次 ps」，量级差 50–150 倍。这直接违反工程红线①静默经济（无固定频率子进程派生）。
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.evidence: listing.go:58-63 `for _, e := range entries { ... prov = identify(e.pane.PanePID) }`；server.go:297 `snap := buildSnapshot(s.catalog, s.identifyProvider)`；whitelist.go:12 `return s.providerFinder.Identify(panePID)`；proctree.go:44 `snap := f.snapshot([]int{panePID})`；proctree.go:77-89 `key := paneSetKey(panePIDs) ... if f.snap != nil && f.paneKey == key && time.Since(f.snap.taken) < procTTL { return f.snap }`；proctree.go:107 `exec.Command("ps", "-axo", "pid=,ppid=,comm=")`。实测（git archive dc9aab11b 到 /private/tmp/claude-501/audit-jank 后跑）：IdentifySet(10 pid) 之后再 Identify 这 10 个 pid，重新 fork 全表 10 次、耗时 487ms；模拟 3 个 tick，每 tick 恰好 11 次 fork；而基线形状（只 IdentifySet，键不变）5 个 tick 重新 fork 0 次。本机 `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,comm= | wc -l` = 906 行，单次 ps 实测 48ms。

ab2c3d5995849e4ef.title: 缓存键被单 pid 覆盖，连下一 tick 的 IdentifySet 也失去 TTL 复用
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.claim: `f.paneKey = key` 在每次单 pid Identify 后被写成 `"<pid>"`，于是下一个 tick 的 `IdentifySet(全部pid)` 键也对不上，即使距上次采样不到 10s（procTTL）也强制重采。缓存的 TTL 语义在新调用形状下被完全废掉，不只是「多 N 次」，而是「连原来那 1 次的复用也没了」。
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.failure_scenario: N=10、tick 间隔 2s：基线下 IdentifySet 的键恒定，10s TTL 内 5 个 tick 只 fork 1 次；改后每个 tick 固定 11 次 fork（实测 tick0/1/2 = 11/11/11），TTL 分支一次都没命中过。
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.evidence: proctree.go:76-89 `func (f *procFinder) snapshot(panePIDs []int) *procSnap { key := paneSetKey(panePIDs); ... f.snap = snap; f.paneKey = key }`；实测 TestAuditPerTickForkCount 三个 tick 各 11 次 fork，无一次 TTL 命中。最小根因修法：把 paneKey 判据换成「TTL 未过期 且 请求的每个 pid 都在 snap.parent 里」，删掉 paneKey 字段——新 pane 出现时 pid 不在表里仍会强制重采，行为不弱于现状，且 Identify/IdentifySet 两个调用方一起修好（符合「修在所有调用方都经过的地方」）。

ab2c3d5995849e4ef.title: handleList 在连接读循环上同步跑这轮扫描，阻塞其后所有帧 → 进屏白屏
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.claim: handleFrame 在 readLoop 里同步分发，handleList 直接调 `refreshListing`（= rebuildCatalog = 上面那 N+1 次 ps）。这条连接在扫描期间处理不了任何后续帧，包括 app 在 sendList() 紧接着发出的 subscribe/level2_subscribe。

ab2c3d5995849e4ef.evidence: ws_conn.go:134-150 readLoop 里 `if !c.handleFrame(data)`；ws_conn.go:367-370 `switch t := typed.(type) { case protocol.List: c.handleList(t)`（同步，无 goroutine）；ws_handler.go:79 `err := c.s.refreshListing(c.ctx)`；server.go:380 `if err := s.rebuildCatalog(ctx); err != nil`；ConnectionManager.kt:693-695 `setState(READY); sendList(); replaySubscriptions(reconnect)`。修复方向：让 handleList 复用最近一次快照（或把重扫挪到独立 goroutine 并异步回 listing），至少不要让它落在 readLoop 上。

ab2c3d5995849e4ef.title: 过滤用的 provider 判定与打标用的 provider 判定来自两张不同时刻的 ps 表，可制造每 tick 都有 ChangedSessions 的 list_delta
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.claim: filterModel 用 T 时刻的 IdentifySet 结果决定哪些 pane 入列，buildSnapshot 用 T+k（k 为该 pane 之前所有 pane 的 ps 耗时之和，N=30 时可达 1s+）的另一张 ps 表决定 Session.Provider。两者不一致时，Provider 会在 tick 之间翻动；而 diff 的变更判据是整个 struct 比较 `old != cur`（Provider 是 struct 字段），一次翻动就产生一条 ChangedSessions。
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.failure_scenario: 某个 pane 的 provider 判定依赖子进程（如 cursor 靠 node 路径段、claude 靠子进程 comm），若在 filterModel 与轮到它的 Identify 之间该子进程刚好不在表里，则该 tick Provider 为空、下一 tick 又恢复 ⇒ 连续两个 tick 各发一条 ChangedSessions 的 list_delta，app 侧列表反复重组。注意：我没有观测到实际翻动样本，这是结构性可能，不是已复现事实。
ab2c3d5995849e4ef.evidence: server.go:295-297 `s.catalog.rebuild(filterModel(s, model))` 紧接 `buildSnapshot(s.catalog, s.identifyProvider)`，两处各自触发独立的 readProcTable；listing.go:112-118 `if old != cur { d.ChangedSessions = append(d.ChangedSessions, cur) }`（protocol.Session 含新增的 Provider 字段，listing.go:34 `Provider: provider`）。修复方向与 P0 同一处：rebuildCatalog 里把 identifyModel 的 hits map 算一次，filterModel 与 buildSnapshot 共用同一张表——既消掉 N 次 ps，也消掉这个不一致窗口。

a45bb4b459b329a80.title: srv-first-frame: pipe attaches AFTER Resize, so the SIGWINCH redraw is silently dropped
a45bb4b459b329a80.claim: Moving `br.Subscribe` (pipe-pane attach) to after `br.Resize` opens a window in which every byte the CLI writes in response to SIGWINCH is written to the pane but captured by neither the snapshot (taken before the resize) nor the pipe (attached after it). For any TUI that *does* redraw on resize — the normal case, not the frozen case the probe pins — the entire post-resize repaint is lost.
a45bb4b459b329a80.failure_scenario: Host pane is 80x24 running an active Claude Code. Phone subscribes with Rows=96 Cols=108. New order: capture (80x24 content) → Resize to 108x96 → CLI receives SIGWINCH and repaints the whole screen at 108x96 → `br.Subscribe` attaches pipe-pane only now, so that repaint is never relayed. The phone renders the 80-col snapshot inside a 108-col emulator (`emulator.replaySnapshot(frame.data, emulator.cols, emulator.rows)`), i.e. text crammed into the left 80 columns with the old wrap points, and it stays that way until the CLI happens to emit something else — indefinitely if the CLI is idle waiting for input.
a45bb4b459b329a80.evidence: pr/srv-first-frame ws_handler.go:151-171 — the diff deletes the comment `// Attach the pipe before the snapshot so no output between the two is lost (term-bridge knowledge base: pipe first, then capture).` and reorders to capture→Resize→Subscribe. The invariant is still asserted as fact in the module it belongs to: server/internal/bridge/stream.go:7-9 `Subscribe order is fixed by the knowledge base: the pipe is attached before the caller grabs a snapshot, so no output between the two is ever lost`, and stream.go:142 `Attach the pipe before the snapshot so no output can slip between this call and the snapshot the caller takes next.` Neither doc was updated by the branch.

a45bb4b459b329a80.title: srv-first-frame: only the frozen-TUI world is pinned; nothing pins the redrawing-TUI world
a45bb4b459b329a80.claim: The probe's fixture is a script whose WINCH trap clears and never redraws (`trap 'printf "\033[2J\033[H" > /dev/tty' WINCH` then blocks on read). It therefore can only distinguish 'snapshot empty' from 'snapshot has glyphs'; it is green both under the fix and under any future change, and it is structurally incapable of catching the lost-redraw regression above. No test in the branch subscribes a pane that emits output on SIGWINCH and asserts those bytes reach the client.
a45bb4b459b329a80.failure_scenario: Someone reverts or re-reorders the capture/Resize/Subscribe triple in a way that loses live output; `go test ./internal/api -run StaticAltScreenFirstFrame` still passes because the fixture never emits anything after subscribe. The full-suite green in .team/nodes/hl1-sfix/tmp/go-full.log likewise proves nothing about the active-TUI path.
a45bb4b459b329a80.evidence: pr/srv-first-frame server/internal/api/hl092_static_alt_first_frame_probe_test.go:34-40 defines `frozenAltScript` with the clear-only WINCH trap; the only assertion (lines 63-80) is that the *first* KindSnapshot within 2s contains `staticAltMarker`. There is no read of subsequent frames and no assertion about deltas.

a45bb4b459b329a80.title: srv-first-frame contradicts handleResize, which still captures right after Resize
a45bb4b459b329a80.claim: The branch changes handleSubscribe on the premise that a capture taken right after Resize is empty for an idle alt-screen TUI, but leaves handleResize doing exactly that, with a comment asserting the opposite premise.
